Sen. Kevin Cramer says Nvidia ($NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang should step down, citing national security and potential Chinese blackmail risks.

text:
4 days, 20+ meetings and one site visit at IMARC 2026.

My key takeaways:

• Jurisdiction is half the story. From the US to Paraguay, Ecuador, Guyana, Chile: where the asset sits shapes my gut feel as much as the rock.

• What's the second asset? Plenty of single-asset juniors were perfectly fine, but there was nothing beyond the one project to get excited about.

• Loved seeing a prospect generator/royalty hybrid. Will follow that thread.

• More deal talk than investment talk. Partnerships, JVs, finding the right vehicle, rather than just "buy my stock".

• Canada in the house! Plenty of North American groups in Sydney looking at Australia and at cross-border deals.

• Grades keep falling. Chile's copper ore grade went from 1.29% to 0.58% between 2000 and 2025 (Cochilco), and the fix may start with sensors reading grade in real time.

All in all, another excellent event.

Great to catch up with friends, companies, and clients including the @StGeorge_SGQ team at their stand. Rare earths and niobium, front and centre 💪

text:
$PENG - BofA hosted CEO Kash Shaikh and management, and came away more convinced.

Buy and $100 price target reiterated, with estimates unchanged. The stock is at ~$49.

Key takeaways from the meeting:

Growth is broadening
It’s no longer just memory. Growth is spreading across AI infrastructure and integrated memory. Penguin has managed 100K+ GPUs and 4.2bn GPU runtime hours, and that operating experience is the edge against OEMs and system integrators.

Services and software are the moat
• Customer contracts of 3–5 years with uptime SLAs
• ClusterWare monitors clusters and fixes issues automatically
• ClusterWare AI adds an agentic layer, priced per GPU
• Works across hardware vendors, so customers aren’t locked into one platform

Inference is a memory story
Bigger models, longer context windows and AI agents all need more memory. Penguin’s CXL-based MemoryAI and KV-cache products move data off scarce HBM, which cuts recomputation and improves token economics. It’s also building a photonics memory appliance with $MRVL to pool memory across racks.

Discipline over growth at any cost
Management is selective with neoclouds, looking at real demand, equity backing, power and financing before signing. The focus is EPS and operating leverage, not maximizing revenue.

The numbers (BofA, FY Aug)
- FY27 EPS $4.81 vs $4.57 consensus
- FY28 EPS $5.43
- ~10x FY27 and ~9x FY28 earnings at today’s price

What to watch is: working capital. 

BofA has FY27 free cash flow at just $69M on $30

text:
I disagree, Jensen Huang is practically irreplaceable from $NVDA.

And it's like if you took out Elon from $TSLA, the valuation and confidence in the company would collapse. 

The foresight to bet on CUDA before AI took off, build the Neocloud ecosystem... 

The move to secure critical supply chain capacity years ahead of demand, and sell rack-scale systems (with CPUs, networking, etc). 

Turn the ASIC threat into another opportunity by investing in $MRVL, MediaTek, to compete against $AVGO. Bringing them all into Nvidia's NVLink ecosystem... 

Is absolutely insane foresight. Jensen practically architected both the financial and industrial ecosystem surrounding the current AI trade. 

Jensen took Nvidia from a startup to a $5T+ company, and the fact he managed to keep growing that with projected FY2028 70% constrained forward growth... at these levels.

Is equally as absurd. 

I normally don't post negative things about companies... but even if you don't see material revenue or roadmap changes in the next 2 years. 

Ousting the face of the AI trade and a technology visionary might spell disaster for Nvidia long term.

text:
Who decides Jensen Huang's fate at $NVDA?

X is full of strong opinions. Let's look at the facts.
Then I'll share what I believe is currently happening behind the scenes.

There are 11 directors on the board.
Jensen is the only one who isn't independent.
Removing him takes a simple majority for the decision: 6 votes.

Nvidia has no chair. Lead independent director Stephen Neal (77, a white-collar defense lawyer) runs the process.

The 10 independent directors (number in bracket represents an estimate how much money they made from NVDIA stock).

The founding loyalists:
1) Mark Stevens (since 1993, ~$7.5B): Sequoia partner when it backed Nvidia in 1993. Sold ~$1.4B of stock this year.
2) Tench Coxe (1993, ~$5.9B): Sutter Hill co-led Nvidia's first $2M round.
3) Harvey Jones (1993, ~$1.6B): advised Jensen in the earliest days.
4) Brooke Seawell (1997, ~$0.6B): has chaired the audit committee for decades.

Jensen made them ~$15.6B. They've known Jensen for 30+ years.

The swing votes:
5) Stephen Neal (2019, ~$38M): his old firm Cooley has been Nvidia's outside counsel since 1993, but he's a career white-collar investigator.
6) Dawn Hudson (2013, ~$162M): chairs the committee that sets Jensen's pay.
7) Aarti Shah (2020, ~$12M): her son works at Nvidia.

The independents:
8) John Dabiri (2020, ~$6M): Caltech academic.
9) Melissa Lora (2023, ~$3M): has never sold a share.
10) Suzanne Nora Johnson (July 2026, ~$0): joined from Goldman Sachs.

Ousting Jensen needs all 3 independents A

SpaceX simply figured out how to do it at scale.

- Optical companies like $POET traded -$97M under net cash. Valuing the operating business very negatively, not even at $0.
